verdict: RUNG (local census reproduces gate1.argmax_census on identical starts): 6 models compared, worst error 0.00e+00. Bit-identical, so the only thing that differs below is WHERE THE STARTS COME FROM. PRIMARY, does the BOS domain effect survive in-distribution starts? Falcon3-1B-Base: random +0.693 (tol 0.083) vs text +0.714 (tol 0.042) -> survives; Minerva-3B-base-v1.0: random -0.323 (tol 0.042) vs text -0.359 (tol 0.063) -> survives; pythia-410m-deduped: random -0.422 (tol 0.042) vs text -0.536 (tol 0.063) -> survives; Qwen1.5-1.8B: random -0.510 (tol 0.042) vs text -0.239 (tol 0.167) -> survives; SmolLM-1.7B: random -0.562 (tol 0.125) vs text -0.667 (tol 0.208) -> survives; Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct: random -0.562 (tol 0.042) vs text -0.490 (tol 0.062) -> survives. Survives on 6, collapses or reverses on 0, untestable on 0 of 6. The domain effect is NOT an out-of-distribution artefact on these models: it survives when the loop is seeded with real bigrams. F66's warning does not extend to this readout, and paper 2's claims stand as drafted. SECONDARY, phi under text starts vs random starts on the RAW arm: Falcon3-1B-Base 0.214 -> 0.250 (+0.036); Minerva-3B-base-v1.0 0.328 -> 0.422 (+0.094); pythia-410m-deduped 0.427 -> 0.536 (+0.109); Qwen1.5-1.8B 0.510 -> 0.240 (-0.271); SmolLM-1.7B 0.562 -> 0.667 (+0.104); Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct 0.573 -> 0.495 (-0.078). 1 of 6 models shift by >= 0.20, so the two start distributions are not probing the same object and the PRIMARY must be read as a comparison between two regimes rather than a robustness check within one. BOUNDARY: 6 models, ONE text source (Pile rows 0-39), ONE prefix kind (BOS), 2 census seeds, 96 starts. 'In-distribution' here means adjacent pairs from one corpus, not representative of use. The local census is gate1's, proven by the RUNG rather than assumed.
